# Public proof materials

Keep this folder limited to public construction data, reproducible verification
source, and proof records. Do not add manuscript sources, PDFs, bibliographies,
draft figures, Git history, compiled binaries, or unrelated search diaries.

Keep the catalogue and docs/data-map.json consistent. Preserve all mathematical
inputs, witnesses, search settings, completion outcomes, and coverage information.
Public records are metadata-normalized copies; untouched research records are
maintained outside this folder. Do not add calendar dates, development-history
labels, dated paths, job identifiers, host names, or personal filesystem paths.
Elapsed computational durations and literature attribution may be retained.

Update linked digests and SHA256SUMS.json for intentional public changes, then
run verify_all.py. A recorded binary fingerprint must never be described as
verification of an omitted binary. Do not overwrite the separate research
repository or manuscript. Do not upload remotely without the author's request.

# Regular logical frames: expanded proof workspace

Only constructions and supporting evidence explicitly used by the paper and
its appendices are included. The catalogue contains 40 entries; four additional
constructions use dedicated proof packages. See [the catalogue](docs/CATALOGUE.md)
and [the claim map](docs/data-map.json).

```sh
python3 verify.py
python3 verify_all.py
```

Python 3.10+ and a C++17 compiler suffice. The first command reconstructs all
catalogue examples, checks canonical frames and witnesses, and verifies file
integrity. The second runs all finite proof audits and small-instance engine
tests; it does not rerun the deep exhaustive searches. Each package README gives
its reproduction commands. [Verification](docs/VERIFICATION.md) and
[packaging](docs/PACKAGING.md) explain the evidence boundaries.

Discovery campaigns, unreported examples, ancillary extensions, manuscript
files, Git history, and compiled binaries are outside this release.

## How to cite

If you use or adapt the code constructions, logical-frame methods, or
distance-search and certification method, please cite the accompanying paper:

> Jong Yeon Lee, *Designing Group-Valued Codes with Full Regular Low-Weight Bases*
> (2026), [arXiv:2610.06820](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06820) [quant-ph].

### Efficient distance search and exact certification for LP codes

Please cite the paper when using or extending its method for efficient exhaustive
distance certification of lifted-product (LP) codes, including in independent
implementations. The method combines translation-symmetry reduction,
syndrome-directed branching, and stabilizer-overlap pruning to reduce the search
while preserving the lower-bound guarantee. The paper gives the completeness
arguments and demonstrates exact certification for LP examples with more than
a thousand physical qubits.

Searches on smaller constituent and quotient codes help reject weak candidates
early. Exact quantum distance requires completed full-code exclusions below the
weight of a verified logical witness, covering both CSS sectors or using a
verified sector-exchange symmetry. The method and its relation to prior work are
described in the paper's LP section and Appendix A.

Suggested attribution, when applicable:

> We use the exhaustive distance-certification method of Lee, combining
> translation-symmetry reduction with syndrome-directed branching and
> stabilizer-overlap pruning.

### BibTeX

```bibtex
@misc{lee2026designinggroupvaluedcodesregular,
  title         = {Designing Group-Valued Codes with Full Regular Low-Weight Bases},
  author        = {Jong Yeon Lee},
  year          = {2026},
  eprint        = {2610.06820},
  archivePrefix = {arXiv},
  primaryClass  = {quant-ph},
  url           = {https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06820}
}
```

If you use the released implementation, constructions, or proof data, please
also cite the repository:

```bibtex
@misc{LeeRegularFramesSoftware,
  author = {Lee, Jong Yeon},
  title  = {regular-logical-frames: Constructions and Computational Proof Data},
  url    = {https://github.com/yeon-lee/public-regular-logical-frames},
  note   = {Software and computational proof data}
}
```

[CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff) provides machine-readable citation metadata.

# Export and reproduce a distance search

From the folder root:

```sh
python3 codes/reproduce_distance.py lp-f2-320-64-10 --output /tmp/lp320.txt
python3 codes/reproduce_distance.py lp-f2-320-64-10 --output /tmp/lp320.txt --run --seconds 3600
```

The first command verifies the physical construction and exports complete
logical detectors. The second compiles the archived C++17 engine and excludes
through the claimed distance minus one, retaining a fresh receipt and logs
beside the requested output. These are new run files, not replacements for
preserved evidence.

All catalogue IDs are accepted, including odd-period comparisons with residual
logical classes. The script checks every required root and rejects incomplete
or partitioned terminal output. A timeout or a lighter witness establishes no
new lower bound. 

For the largest examples use the dedicated package commands in the
[proof guide](../docs/VERIFICATION.md); their symmetry reductions and specialized
pruning can be faster. Recorded execution records and physical witnesses
remain distinct from formal node-by-node proof objects.

# lp-f4-476-56-14

This is the self-adjoint quaternary lifted-product code `[[476,56,14]]`,
with a full regular canonical frame of width 20. The width is achieved; its
optimality is not asserted. The constituent, selected pivot columns, physical
checks, seed supports and distance witness are given in this directory.

From the repository root, reconstruct and verify the code and its frame:

```sh
python3 verify.py --code lp-f4-476-56-14
```

Validate the preserved exhaustive execution, its input binding, all translation
roots and the upper witness:

```sh
python3 codes/lp-quaternary/lp-f4-476-56-14/proof/replay.py
```

Recompile the preserved C++17 source and rerun the full lower-bound search:

```sh
python3 codes/lp-quaternary/lp-f4-476-56-14/proof/replay.py --run --seconds 90 --output /tmp/lp-f4-476-56-14-replay
```

The script locates all inputs relative to itself and works from any current
working directory. The original receipt preserves recorded command strings;
those absolute strings are not used by validation or replay. `receipt.json` is
an explicitly labelled portable normalization. No original machine paths or
external search folders are required.

The search input uses all three nonzero binary combinations of each F4 check.
The replay validator checks equality of these check and stabilizer spaces with
the published independent binary rows and binds every logical detector to the
reconstructed complete frame. It accepts only a completed, unsharded search over
all 68 translation roots and every child branch through weight
13. A verified weight-preserving block transpose transfers the Z-sector
lower bound to X. A timeout is not a lower bound.

`proof/replayed/` records an independent fresh compilation and full rerun made
when this portable package was prepared. These execution records are distinct
from a formally machine-checked proof object; the source and complete replay
inputs are included for inspection.

# Published odd-period LP comparison

The retained [[1122,148,20]] example has a partial regular frame covering 132
of 148 logical pairs, with width 44. The remaining 16 classes are represented
in the complete logical detectors used by the distance search. The partial
width supplies no upper bound on optimized full-code frame width.
`python3 comparisons/check.py` checks its physical construction and scope.

# Data conventions

A cyclic frame is stored as seed pairs. Translating each pair by t^g in pair
order and then g=0,...,P-1 gives the full basis. Translation sends binary
coordinate block*P+j to block*P+(j+1 mod P). The noncyclic package uses tuple
addition modulo 16 and modulo 2.

For F4, integers 0,1,2,3 denote 0,1,omega,omega^2 with omega^2=omega+1.
The self-dual trace basis (omega,omega^2) expands a quaternary coordinate into
binary blocks 2*block and2*block+1. The involution reverses group exponents and
fixes field coefficients. A term t^e sends position j to j+e.

LP constituent entries are lists of [exponent,coefficient] terms; an empty list
is zero. Physical blocks are ordered first by a*s+b in the s*s block, then by
s*s+i*r+j in the r*r block. Pivot columns are explicit. Quaternary LP checks
select the lightest two of binary row 0, row 1, and their sum, breaking ties in
that order. PP records store coefficient/exponent arrays; a zero coefficient
means a zero block regardless of its exponent.

In code.json, frame_width.upper is the weight of the supplied full canonical
frame, not an optimality claim unless optimal=true. regular_frame_width, when
present, refers to the specified cyclic action. The five comparison entries
instead use partial_frame.width and explicitly retain 16 residual logical pairs;
that partial width is not a full-frame upper bound. A null bound means no bound
of that type is supplied.

Research and manuscript: Jong Yeon Lee. Numerical candidate development and
verification used AI assistance as described in the paper. The invertible-pivot
LP tensor basis specializes Bhardwaj et al., arXiv:2607.28795, Appendix B,
Theorem 4. PP cofactor seeds use Okada and Kasai, arXiv:2609.35601, Sec. 2.3.
Published comparison inputs retain their attribution in their code records.

records.content:
# Public packaging conventions

This package contains metadata-normalized copies of construction and verification
materials. Calendar dates, workstation paths, scheduler identifiers, and manuscript
revision labels are omitted. Filenames identify their mathematical role rather
than a development date. The author retains the untouched source records separately.

Coefficient and exponent arrays, physical matrices, logical supports, search
cutoffs, root and shard parameters, exit status, terminal results, node counts,
and coverage information are preserved. Exploratory candidate-selection and
heuristic sampling seeds are omitted, as are site-specific deployment helpers.
Distance exclusions start from the supplied
physical matrices and retain their deterministic coverage settings. Independent
ring-arithmetic spot checks use the documented fixed seed zero.

Elapsed durations describe computational
cost and are not calendar timestamps. Literature identifiers retain attribution.

All distributed hashes bind the normalized public files. Metadata normalization
changes file digests; it does not establish a new execution or convert an execution
record into a formal proof. The independent checkers still test algebra, witnesses,
settings, transcript agreement, and complete required coverage. Large exclusions
are reproduced only by explicitly running their documented search commands.

Compiled executables are omitted. [EXECUTABLE_IDENTITIES.json](EXECUTABLE_IDENTITIES.json)
retains the fingerprints declared in execution records so that agreement across
records remains checkable. That agreement does not independently verify binary
contents or establish that a binary was built from the supplied source. The
`evidence_digest` helper explicitly distinguishes hashing an included file from
looking up an omitted executable's declaration. Portable replay builds from source.

No incomplete execution is credited as an exclusion. Some interrupted-prefix
records are retained because the coverage checker uses their completed subtrees;
only a checked union of complete intervals supports the corresponding lower bound.

# Verification and reproduction

Run `python3 verify.py` for physical reconstruction, all canonical pairings,
logical witnesses, and integrity. Run `python3 verify_all.py` for the complete
finite suite, including proof-pool/coloring checks, recorded exclusion coverage,
small-instance engine tests, and the PP shallow-frontier replay. Python 3.10+
and a C++17 compiler suffice. The suite does not rerun large exhaustive searches.

[data-map.json](data-map.json) maps every reported construction and computational
claim to its input, checker, and proof records. Each proof package's README gives
fresh-run commands; the generic [distance runner](../codes/REPRODUCING_DISTANCES.md)
also accepts every catalogue ID. Replays compile from the supplied source and
must finish all required roots and partitions before establishing a lower bound.

The release retains 40 catalogue records plus four specialized constructions:
the independent-constituent LP example, the noncyclic PP example, and the two
sparse PP constructions with check weight eight. Only examples in the paper
or its appendices are included.

A physical witness proves an upper bound. A finite coloring certifies a graph
consequence only after the relevant physical-word pool is complete. Completed
exhaustive executions support lower bounds through the stated algorithm and
coverage records; these are not formal proofs checking every visited node.
The separate minimum-weight LP sector bases are finite, independently checked
certificates. Their existence does not imply canonical pairing under the
specified cyclic action. The PP detector exclusion is distinct from its distance
exclusion. Frame widths remain upper bounds unless optimality is proved.

No incomplete execution is credited as complete. Some interrupted-prefix
records are necessary for checked unions of completed root intervals. Omitted
executables have declared fingerprints, not independently checked contents.
See [packaging conventions](PACKAGING.md).

content.path_convention: All paths are repository-relative. JSON pointers refer to fields within the indicated existing file. Manuscript locations are stable TeX labels, not potentially changing section numbers.

claims.scope: All stored codes and frames, physical upper witnesses and integrity. Per-code evidence pointers route to lower-bound provenance; this command does not rerun distance exclusions.

Physical masks, class coordinates, all relative shifts, graph and proper coloring are independently checked. The coloring consequence assumes pool completeness, established by the separate released enumeration and completed execution records; it is not a formal search proof object. The supplied distance-weight regular sector bases, together with the certified distances, give f_span^X = f_span^Z = d. The canonical lower bounds concern the prescribed C16 action; unrestricted f remains unresolved.

Finite detector/frame checks, all 64 completion records, small-instance tests and optional shallow frontier replay. The prefix audit does not rerun the deep detector-odd exclusion through 24. Its completed execution is not a formal proof object; this is distinct from the ordinary distance exclusion through 23. The detector exclusion also gives f_span^Z >= 25; the supplied frame gives f_span = f = f_reg = 25. This is a deduction from the same completed exclusion and finite frame data, not a new search.

claims.catalogue_membership: Separate noncyclic package; not included in entry_count or the cyclic-code catalogue.
claims.scope: The noncyclic C16 x C2 CSS construction has [[512,128,19]], maximum check weight 10, maximum column weight 4, and an achieved full regular canonical frame width of 25. The finite checker verifies physical checks, all 32 translates of four binary seed pairs, canonical Gram matrix I128, the weight-19 witness and completed-search coverage. Exact distance uses the recorded completed exhaustive exclusion through 18 (360294418 node visits); auditing records is not a formal node-by-node proof. Width 25 is an upper bound, with unrestricted optimized width only bounded between 19 and 25.
Dense independent constituents give exact [[544,64,14]], maximum check weight9 and achieved full regular frame width16. Both CSS sectors have complete exclusions through weight13.

Q16 has exact [[1088,128,22]], check maximum 10 and column maximum 6. All eight binary X and eight Z seeds have weight 22, so the full regular canonical frame attains d and proves f=f_reg=22. The quick check reconstructs the physical code/frame and audits all 64 completed exclusion shards through 21; it does not rerun the deep search. The 781613767-node execution and verified sector isometry establish the lower bound; records are not formal node-by-node proof traces.

Q17 and Q18 have exact parameters [[544,64,14]] and [[1088,128,16]], check maximum 8 and column maximum 5. Achieved full regular frame widths 22 and 26 are upper bounds, not optimality claims. Each preserved exclusion covers all 68 normalized roots through d-1; physical witnesses and a verified sector-transpose isometry establish both sector distances. Both exclusions also passed fresh portable compiled replays, with 731629 and 2428976 nodes respectively. Quick mode checks completed execution records without repeating the search.

claims.catalogue_membership: Dedicated verification package; these two examples are not included in entry_count or the cyclic-code catalogue.
claims.scope: Sparse cyclic PP examples have exact [[512,128,11]] and [[1024,256,12]], check maximum 8, column maximum 4, and achieved full regular frame widths 16 and 15. The checker reconstructs physical checks, all translated canonical pairings, witnesses, redundant check rowspaces and the sector reflection; it audits all 16 completed cyclic roots, first-branch coverage and hashes. Widths are not proved optimal, and the sparse search is incomplete. Completed execution audits are not formal node-by-node proof traces.

Exact [[768,192,20]], check weight9, column weight4, achieved full regular frame width30. All64 matching weight19 hash shards cover all16 translation roots (394443504 node visits); a verified attaining witness and sector reflection give d_X=d_Z=20. The unit-pivot check is explicit at period48. Quick auditing does not revisit deep search nodes; --replay compiles and repeats the exclusion. Width30 is not proved optimal.

Exact [[768,192,13]] and [[768,192,12]], both with check weight8 and column weight4; achieved regular-frame widths20 and15. Both full exclusions were freshly replayed from portable source. No frame optimum or family-wide distance ceiling is asserted.

P48 construction with exact distance22, w10, wc5 and achieved full regular frame width29. All64 disjoint weight21 exclusion pieces completed with verified identities and full frontier coverage; the physical weight22 logical attains the bound. Width29 is not claimed optimal.
Parent CSS distance24: physical witness, sector reflection, all64 completed shards and source/input binding. No folded-code distance claim is included.
Five fully populated cyclic 512-qubit constructions reported in the paper.

# Completed proof evidence

Only inputs and execution evidence needed by the reported examples are retained.
Construction recipes, canonical seeds, and witnesses are indexed in the catalogue;
[the claim map](../docs/data-map.json) identifies specialized packages.
Exact engines, terminal records, and root/partition coverage permit reproduction.
Execution records are not formal node-by-node proof objects.
